faq.a: MCP lets an AI call tools. It says nothing about who the AI is, what it may do, or what it passed on. Supabrain adds identity and rules (ENS) and a signed record (Arkiv), enforced on every MCP call.
We catch the common shapes, but no detector catches everything. That's why every AI also has hard ENS limits: paths, writes per day, on or off. A missed injection still can't write outside its scope.

faq.q: Why ENS rather than a config file?
faq.a: A config file can be changed silently by whoever runs the server. ENS rules are public, owned by the project owner, and every change is an on-chain transaction anyone can see.
With a database, "Gemini wrote this" means "trust us". On Arkiv, the AI's own wallet signs it, nobody can edit it, and anyone can check it without our server.
It's kept for the owner's review and revoked on Arkiv with a public revocation. No AI receives it, and history isn't rewritten.

faq.q: What if someone pastes a real API key?
faq.a: It's refused before writing. Nothing reaches the chain.
We sponsor it: rule changes on Sepolia and writes on Arkiv. Users don't need tokens.
The ones on the Connect page: Claude Code, the Claude app, Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Codex and ChatGPT developer mode. We only list what has a tested snippet.
Everything except the landing page's scroll story, which is labelled as an example. Every number and link comes from the live server, ENS on Sepolia and Arkiv.

limits: The content check is a pattern tripwire, not a classifier. It catches the common shapes of injection: overriding instructions, piping a remote script into a shell, redirecting payments, asking for secrets, rewriting one's own rules and commanding another AI. Wording it doesn't recognise can pass. That is why the ENS rules exist: they limit what any AI can do regardless of what it read.
Real secrets (private keys, PEM keys, API tokens) are refused before writing and never reach the chain. Requests for secrets are stopped.

For the demo, the server holds the AIs' wallets (derived from one secret, gas sponsored). The supabrain.eth owner key stays offline; the server's key can only manage the brain registries and the AI resolvers.
The attack lab runs as the brain owner, because every write is a real Arkiv transaction. Visitors see every result live, read-only.
Testnets only (Ethereum Sepolia, Arkiv Rabdi), with synthetic data.
